newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian tax service, Norilsk agree payment deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian tax service, Norilsk agree payment deal.

text.p: The Russian Tax Inspectorate has agreed a schedule of payment of back taxes with copper and nickel producer Norilsk Nickel and has no intention of freezing metal or property, a top tax official said on Thursday.
"This is not just talk. We have signed documents," Vitaly Gunbin, head of the tax inspectorate for Krasnoyarsk region, where the metals producer is located, told Reuters by telephone.
"We have agreed they will pay a bit more than 140 billion roubles per month in November and December," he said.
Total debts of the Norilsk Combine, the main producer of copper and nickel and chief component company of RAO Norilsk Nickel, were 500 billion roubles, he said.
Gunbin said he would meet Norilsk authorities again towards the New Year to schedule the rest of the debt.
"They are able to pay. This should not scare you," he told Reuters. He did not say whether Norilsk would have to pay the taxes in cash.
"We have settled all questions between us and we (the tax service) have withdrawn all intentions (to freeze metal)."
Gunbin said he had made the deal with Norilsk Combine director Nikolai Abramov.
On Wednesday press reports said tax authorities had frozen millions of dollars worth of metal from the factory.
A Norilsk spokesman on Wednesday told Reuters that the authorities had only threatened action.
Gunbin said that his service had begun proceedings to freeze metal for the last half month.
But he said the metal in question was in the process of refinement, not ready for shipment, and only ready for shipment about Thursday, when the agreement was signed.
"It was waiting for transport," he said, adding that Norilsk's shipments had not been disrupted.
